# The appointments Ọṣun made — and who is keeping them

Take Ọṣun's stories in sequence. They are not episodes; they are appointments — and the modern trades are keeping them.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Ọṣun
- **Pantheon:** Yoruba
- **Domain of influence:** Love, Freshwater, Fertility
- **Pattern seats:** 7
- **Sectors touched:** Home & Lifestyle · Energy & Natural World · Society & Spirit · Health & Wellbeing · Culture & Entertainment
- **Strongest seat:** Beauty, Fashion & Cosmetics
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 183 of 271

## The Cycle, Read Forward

### Beauty, Fashion & Cosmetics — through *Ọṣun and the Failed World*

When the male orishas set out to create the world, they ignored Ọṣun.  Their work collapsed: what they built fell apart, what they planted withered, and what they decided proved unjust.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Beauty, sweetness, and adornment; the river that gilds.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. Industries do not invent their archetypes; they inherit them and call them best practice.

### Love, Dating & Relationships — through *The Òṣun River and Oshogbo*

The city of Oshogbo was founded where Ọṣun appeared to a hunter and the first king, establishing the sacred grove that is now a UNESCO World Heritage site.  The river is not merely her symbol; it is believed to be her body.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The sweet river of love; attraction as fresh water.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. That is the cycle working: story becomes duty, duty becomes trade.

### Freshwater & Hydrology — through *Ọṣun and Ṣàngó*

Ọṣun is one of Ṣàngó's wives, and their pairing joins fire and water.  In one story, Ọṣun wins Ṣàngó's love by feeding him honey and by being the only one who can calm his rage.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The sweet river itself; freshwater as love, fertility, and livelihood.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. The trade thinks it is optimizing a process. It is re-enacting a charter.

### Agriculture, Food & Harvest — through *Ọṣun and the Failed World*

When the male orishas set out to create the world, they ignored Ọṣun.  Their work collapsed: what they built fell apart, what they planted withered, and what they decided proved unjust.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Freshwater fertility; the river that sweetens the crop.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. The trade thinks it is optimizing a process. It is re-enacting a charter.

## The Theme That Runs the Cycle

Ọṣun's stories are told in Ifá verses, river rituals, and the annual Oshogbo festival. They centre on the power of sweetness, the necessity of women's wisdom, and the river as a living goddess.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

None of this is numerology. A seat exists only where the match can be argued from the deity’s documented domains and deeds — weighted, published, and falsifiable. The derivation, the weights, and the challenge process are public on the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). If a seat in this file reads wrong, the atlas itself tells you how to prove it — and the correction becomes part of the record.

## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in beauty, fashion & cosmetics, love, dating & relationships, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/sites/oshun/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
